oneLiner: A retailer, ad network and the largest cloud in one P&L, where the market is betting that AWS's sold-out AI capacity turns ~$220B of 2026 capex into a durable step-up in operating income. Reported EPS is not the test - since mid-2025 it has been inflated by Anthropic marks, so the stock works only if operating income compounds.
thesis: AWS is supply-limited, not demand-limited. Jassy said on Oct 23, 2026 that 2027 capacity is 'largely sold out' and 'a good chunk of 2028' too, on top of the $496B Q2 backlog - capex is being spent against booked work, not hope.

Operating leverage is visible through the spend. Operating margin rose from ~10% to 13.7% over the last four quarters while quarterly capex rose ~50%; AWS earns ~60% of operating income on ~21% of revenue, so mix alone lifts the consolidated margin.

Custom silicon is a second franchise. Amazon has disclosed $225B+ of future Trainium revenue commitments including Anthropic and OpenAI (24/7 Wall St, Oct 2026); every Trainium rack that replaces a merchant GPU keeps gross margin inside AWS.
Advertising and retail fund the buildout. Ads grow mid-20s at software-like margins and North America retail earns ~8%; the non-AWS business is no longer a drag on returns.

latestQuarter.label: Q2 2026 (ended Jun 30, 2026; reported Jul 30, 2026)
points: Net sales $200.6B, +20% YoY (first $200B quarter); Prime Day reportedly moved from July into June, pulling sales into Q2.
AWS $42.2B, +36.7% YoY (fastest in 18 quarters), ~39% operating margin; backlog $496B.
Operating income $27.5B, +43% YoY; operating margin 13.7% vs 11.4%.
Diluted EPS $5.75 (net income $62.6B), including $53.4B of pre-tax non-operating gains, primarily the Anthropic stake.
Advertising $19.8B (+26%); North America $116.2B (+16%, 7.9% margin); Q2 capex $53.1B.

segments: North America ~58% of Q2 2026 revenue ($116.2B, +16%, 7.9% operating margin).
AWS ~21% of revenue ($42.2B) but ~60% of operating income ($16.6B of $27.5B).
Advertising $19.8B (+26%), reported inside the geographic segments - the profit mix-shifter.
Strategic stakes: Anthropic ($8B invested through 2025, plus $5B in April 2026 with up to $20B more on milestones), marked up after Anthropic's May 2026 Series H at a reported ~$965B post-money.
competitive: Cloud: Azure grows faster off a smaller base and Google Cloud is gaining; AWS's reacceleration to 37% closed most of the growth gap in 2026.
AI silicon: Trainium vs Nvidia GPUs and Google TPUs; Anthropic co-designs with Annapurna Labs, OpenAI is a second anchor.
Retail: Walmart's e-commerce and Temu/Shein at the low end; fulfillment density keeps Amazon's cost lead.
Advertising: #3 behind Google and Meta, growing faster than both off first-party purchase data.
Satellite: Amazon Leo enters a market Starlink dominates by thousands of satellites.
moat: Prime plus the densest fulfillment network in Western retail is a two-sided lock-in no rival has replicated. AWS adds switching costs, a $496B contracted backlog and proprietary silicon (Trainium, Graviton), while advertising monetizes first-party purchase intent that Google and Meta cannot see.
risks: Capex outruns cash. 2026 capex of ~$220B left trailing free cash flow at about -$7.6B through Q2 2026; if 2027 capex rises again, FCF stays negative for a third year and the return on the buildout is taken on trust.

Earnings quality. Trailing net income is ~144% of operating income because of non-operating gains ($9.5B Q3 2025, $16.8B Q1 2026, $53.4B Q2 2026, mostly Anthropic); headline EPS and trailing P/E flatter the operating business, and the marks can reverse.

Circular demand. Amazon funds Anthropic, Anthropic commits $100B+ to AWS, and the stake mark lifts EPS - if Anthropic's growth or funding stalls, backlog, AWS growth and non-operating income all fall together.
Input-cost inflation. Part of the capex raise to ~$220B was memory prices, not capacity - the same dollars buy less compute, compressing infrastructure ROI and lifting 2027-28 depreciation.
Retail and Leo. A ~8% North America margin leaves little cushion if the consumer weakens; Leo is well short of the FCC's 1,618-satellite July 2026 milestone pending an extension request.
catalysts: Oct 29, 2026 (after close): Q3 2026 report - AWS growth vs ~37%, operating income vs $22.5-26.5B guide, size of non-operating gains, first 2027 capex colour (debates 1, 2, 3).
Early Dec 2026: AWS re:Invent - Trainium3 ramp and Trainium4 roadmap, ~1GW of Trainium capacity for Anthropic by year-end (debate 1).
Anthropic IPO timing (confidential draft filed Jun 2026; listing date unverified) - turns the stake mark into a market price (debate 3).
~Early Feb 2027: Q4 2026 report - formal 2027 capex outlook and full-year FCF (debate 2).

valPresets.note: Basis is forward earnings: FCF is distorted by ~$220B of 2026 capex, and trailing GAAP earnings carry Anthropic marks - forward operating EPS is the cleanest anchor available.

latestProse: Q2 2026 (ended Jun 30; reported Jul 30) was Amazon's first $200B quarter: net sales $200.6B (+20%), helped by Prime Day reportedly moving from July into June. Operating income rose 43% to $27.5B (13.7% margin vs 11.4%), with AWS $42.2B (+36.7%, fastest in 18 quarters) at a ~39% margin and a $496B backlog. Advertising grew 26% to $19.8B; North America grew 16% at a 7.9% margin. Diluted EPS of $5.75 is not an operating number: $53.4B of pre-tax non-operating income, primarily the Anthropic mark after its May Series H, supplied most of the $62.6B of net income. Q2 capex was $53.1B, and trailing free cash flow was about -$7.6B.
guidanceProse: Q3 2026 guide: net sales $197-202B (+9-12% YoY, depressed by the Prime Day timing shift into Q2) and operating income $22.5-26.5B vs $17.4B in Q3 2025. Pre-print consensus sits near the top of the sales range (~$202B) with EPS around $1.96-2.02 - consensus does not model investment marks. Full-year 2026 cash capex was raised to ~$220B from ~$200B, partly on memory-chip prices; no 2027 capex figure has been given. Since the print, Jassy said (Oct 23) that 2027 AWS capacity is largely sold out and a good chunk of 2028 is booked, and that he does not expect the shortage to end in 2027.

verdict.stance: Positive - on operating EPS, not the marks
verdict.summary: Strip out the Anthropic gains and AMZN is a business compounding operating income ~30% a year with AWS capacity sold into 2028, valued on 2027 operating EPS of about $10. The base case returns low-double digits and the bull case (AWS above 35% through 2027 with margin) adds ~45%, against ~30% downside if capex keeps rising while AWS slows - a modestly favourable skew. Two things would change the view: AWS growth falling below 30% while 2027 capex guides higher, or operating income missing the guide in a quarter flattered by marks.
wtb: AWS grows at least 30% YoY in every quarter through Q4 2027 - capacity, not demand, sets the pace.
2027 operating margin reaches at least ~14% (vs ~13% in 2026) despite the depreciation from ~$220B of 2026 capex.
Trailing free cash flow turns positive by Q4 2027, which requires 2027 capex growth well below 2026's ~65%.
The market pays ~28x 2027 operating EPS at end-2027 and gives the Anthropic stake no extra credit.

bear.why: AI capacity is digested: AWS slows to the mid-20s as anchor customers pause, retail softens and 2027 revenue grows ~8% on ~$817B. Depreciation from the 2026 buildout holds net margin at ~10.5%. With FCF still negative the market pays a retail-like multiple.

base.why: AWS grows ~30% as booked capacity comes online, ads ~20%, retail mid-single digits: revenue +13%. Operating margin ~14.5%, net margin ~12.2% after ~17% tax. FCF turns positive late in 2027, so the multiple holds near Amazon's recent range.

bull.why: AWS stays above 35% as Trainium and the sold-out 2028 book convert; revenue +17.5% and AWS mix lifts net margin to ~13.5%. Visible FCF inflection and a second chip franchise earn a low-30s multiple.

scenarioModel.note: 2026 revenue assumes Q1 $181.5B + Q2 $200.6B + ~$200B Q3 (guide midpoint) + ~$235B Q4 = ~$817B. EPS = revenue x net margin / ~10.95B diluted shares (bear 880 x 10.5% = $92.4B; base 925 x 12.2% = $112.9B; bull 960 x 13.5% = $129.6B). EPS excludes non-operating investment marks (Anthropic and other stakes assumed zero), so it will sit well below reported GAAP EPS in any quarter with a mark. Multiples apply to FY2027 EPS at end-2027. Siberforge estimates, not consensus.

debates.bull: Capacity is sold: 2027 largely booked and a good chunk of 2028, a $496B backlog, and $225B+ of Trainium commitments; the constraint is power and chips, not customers.
debates.bear: Two anchor labs (Anthropic, OpenAI) drive much of the backlog; if either slows funding, bookings can be renegotiated and growth reverts to the high-teens of 2024-25.
debates.view: This is the debate that sets the multiple (22x vs 32x). Sold-out commentary is credible for 2027; we need the Q3 print to show acceleration held without the Q2 Prime Day help to retail.

debates.q: Does the capex earn its return, and when does free cash flow turn?
debates.bull: Capex is spent against contracted demand; AWS margins near 39% and rising operating margin show the new capacity earns more than its depreciation.
debates.bear: Trailing FCF is about -$7.6B, part of the 2026 raise is memory-price inflation, and capex intensity is still rising - the cash return keeps moving out a year.
debates.view: Acceptable while AWS margin holds; the bear case starts if 2027 capex rises again without a matching step-up in AWS revenue. Watch the ratio, not the dollar figure.

signpost.metric: 2027 capex outlook vs AWS revenue growth
signpost.threshold: bearish if 2027 capex guided up 25%+ with AWS growth below 30%
signpost.when: Q3 call Oct 29, 2026; formal outlook ~early Feb 2027

debates.q: How much of EPS is Anthropic, and does the stake deserve credit?
debates.bull: The marks are real value: the stake was set by a ~$965B third-party round, and an IPO would give it a market price Amazon could monetize.
debates.bear: Non-operating gains lifted trailing net income to ~144% of operating income; the marks are circular (Amazon funds the customer that buys AWS) and reverse if the valuation falls.
debates.view: We give the stake no credit in the scenarios and value operating EPS only; this debate is upside optionality and an earnings-quality haircut, not the core case.

signpost.metric: Q3 operating income vs guide; size of non-operating gains
signpost.threshold: operating income below the $24.5B guide midpoint while EPS beats on marks = red flag
